expected_behavior: quickLassoActivate() must participate in the same exclusivity mechanism pen and pan already use (arena.tryStart()/arena.end()) instead of setting state.lassoSelectActive directly. The required property is purely behavioral: getActiveGestures().length must never exceed 1, in every order and combination of activation (pen-then-lasso, pan-then-lasso, lasso-then-pen, lasso-then-pan). No particular recognizer is required to 'win' -- a fix that makes lasso participate in the arena and consistently loses to whichever recognizer is already active is just as valid as a fix that makes lasso preempt and cleanly hands off the other recognizer's ownership, as long as the concurrent-active-count invariant holds and normal standalone/lifecycle behavior is preserved.
allowed_repairs: route quickLassoActivate() through arena.tryStart('lasso') (only setting lassoSelectActive if it succeeds), matching the pattern pointerDown() already uses for pen and pan
any equivalent fix that makes lasso's activation consult and participate in the same exclusivity mechanism as pen/pan, in both activation orders

a clean preemption/handoff design (lasso activating cleanly ends whichever other recognizer was active) is also acceptable, provided the invariant (concurrent active count <= 1) holds and lifecycle/standalone behavior is preserved -- winner identity is not scored
forbidden_repairs: disabling lasso select entirely -- caught by lasso_select_works_standalone
disabling pen or pan globally -- caught by pen_draw_works_standalone / pan_canvas_works_standalone

patching lasso only against pen (checking penDrawActive before activating) while leaving the pan+lasso overlap unfixed -- caught by pan_active_then_lasso_condition_stays_exclusive, a genuinely group-wide check
patching lasso only against pan while leaving the pen+lasso overlap unfixed -- caught by pen_active_then_lasso_condition_stays_exclusive

allowing a one-tick overlap that gets cleaned up on a later call -- caught because every assertion snapshots getActiveGestures() immediately after each activation step, not only at a final settled state

changing only arena bookkeeping (e.g. arena's internal activeId) while the actual gesture effect flags (penDrawActive/panCanvasActive/lassoSelectActive) still both remain true -- caught because every assertion reads getActiveGestures(), which is derived from the actual effect flags, never from arena.getActive() directly
permanently locking the first gesture that ever activates, forever -- caught by ending_gesture_releases_slot_and_another_can_start_afterward and repeated_interactions_do_not_leave_stuck_state

globally ignoring all overlapping activation forever after the first conflict is detected once -- caught by lasso_still_works_after_an_earlier_conflict_resolves, which exercises a fresh standalone attempt after a prior conflicting attempt has come and gone

nary_validation.behavioral_invariant: concurrent active gesture count (getActiveGestures().length) never exceeds 1, across the whole 3-participant set, in every reachable ordering
nary_validation.honest_pairwise_representability_stateme: This is NOT a pairwise-valid/triple-only shape like case-017/018. The lasso bypass is universal -- quickLassoActivate() never consults the arena at all, so it breaks exclusivity against EITHER pen OR pan individually, in EITHER activation order (pen_active_then_lasso, pan_active_then_lasso, lasso_active_then_pen, lasso_active_then_pan all fail on the unmodified fixture). Pen vs Pan alone (pen_active_then_pan_condition_stays_exclusive) is already correctly exclusive and is not part of the defect. The genuine N-ary property under test is that all three recognizers belong to one exclusive set and the invariant is enforced group-wide -- not that pairwise checks alone are insufficient to detect the specific bug (they are, in fact, sufficient here, since lasso's bypass is pairwise-observable against either other recognizer). Reporting this as 'all pairs valid, only the triple fails' would be false and is explicitly not claimed.
